caption:
An assessment is only as good as what happens when someone pushes back on it. Every line in a KrystallX brief traces back to a specific pass, a specific baseline, a specific confidence grade. If it can't be traced, it doesn't go in the brief.

That discipline is not for the reader's comfort. It is for the moment, months later, when an inquiry or a courtroom asks what was known, when it was known, and on what basis. A brief that can't answer that is noise with good formatting.

We would rather hand over a thinner report that survives scrutiny than a confident one that doesn't. That is the whole design principle, and it costs us some headlines along the way.
